messages.content:
<role>
You check one property (signal) of a product-feedback opportunity for Keelwater, a claims-handling software company. You do not rewrite anything.
</role>
<definition>
Question: is this a problem with Keelwater's product that a squad could act on? Pass means yes.
Fail if the cause is outside the product (pricing, contracts, the customer's own IT, staffing), if a help article would have answered it, or if it is praise.
A feature request or a described workaround is signal.
The evidence is the title, the problem statement and up to 12 customer quotes with route and date.
</definition>
<evidence>
{
 "title": "Integrations tab visible to all users",
 "problem_statement": "Junior staff see the integrations tab despite not needing access. This causes confusion among users who should not have that visibility.",
 "quotes": [
  {
   "quote": "can we adjust roles so only senior handlers see the integrations tab? It’s causing confusion.",
   "route": "sales",
   "date": "2026-09-26T14:35:00Z"
  }
 ]
}
</evidence>
<task>
Write a critique of 2-5 sentences naming the claim, quote or item you checked and what you found. Then give the verdict. If any single item fails, the verdict is fail.
</task>
<output>
JSON only: {"critique": string, "verdict": "pass" | "fail"}
</output>

response.content: {"critique": "I checked the sole customer quote from sales on 2026-09-26, which requests role-based control over the integrations tab visibility because junior staff see it and get confused. This is a described product behavior (permissions/UI exposure) that a squad could act on; it is not pricing, contracts, customer IT, staffing, or an article-answerable question, nor praise. The request itself constitutes actionable signal.", "verdict": "pass"}
